text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Most European governments that have suspended diplomatic contacts with Bosnia due to the disagreement on distribution of ambassadorial posts will resume those contacts as recommended by the international High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp.
- Jacques Klein, the former U.N. administrator for Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb-held part of Croatia, assumed his new post on Monday as the deputy High Representative to Bosnia.

- Members of the collective presidency have agreed not to appoint ambassadors carrying a burden from wartime, such as possible involvement with corruption or atrocities, said Mirza Hajric, aid to the the presidency chairman.

- Direct telephone links between Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and Serb entity will be established on August 22, said Emin Skopljak, director of the the state telecommunication agency. With only a small number of switches devoted to the link, the capacity set aside for cross-entity calls is far below what is required, he said.
- Bosnia's pension agency will survey the federation to check on the real number of pensioners.

- U.N. spokesman Alex Ivanko said the Agency for Reaserch and Documentation (AID) in Sarajevo will be regarded as a special police unit and treated accordingly under a new policy adopted by the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR), which will now supervise special police units.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic announced on Monday in a televised speech that she will form a new political party which will participate in general elections in the Serb entity scheduled for October 12. -- Sarajevo newsroom ,+387-71-663-864
